reasoning: AtomicFileWrite.swift:31 swaps FileManager.replaceItemAt/moveItem for a bare rename(2). The finding asked for that, and every file in the diff ties back to it: the new AtomicFileWriteTests.swift and the extra check in Validate/main.swift:805-811. The swap also changes how existing files on disk are handled, and nothing pins that. (a) When dest is a symlink, rename replaces the link itself with a regular 0600 file instead of writing through it. The write paths hit are config.toml (ConfigLoader.swift:110,189,276, which includes ensureAllVendorSections on every launch), ~/.codex/auth.json (FileCredentialReader.swift:74, opt-in refresh only), history, pins, and the reset journal. A user who keeps config.toml symlinked to a dotfiles repo silently loses the link on the first write. (b) replaceItemAt preserved the original item's metadata; rename does not. Not following the link on a secret write is arguably the safer choice and fits README:530 ('TOCTOU symlink refusal'), but it needs to be a deliberate, tested decision. None of the 5 tests in AtomicFileWriteTests.swift covers a symlinked destination.
required_changes: Add a test in Tests/AiTaskbarCoreTests/AtomicFileWriteTests.swift for a symlinked destination: the link is replaced by a regular 0600 file and the link target is left unchanged, or the opposite if write-through is what you want.
Document the symlink behaviour in the AtomicFileWrite doc comment and in the README security section (near README.md:522-530), so config.toml users who symlink to dotfiles know what happens.
